assets.subject: Empty American rail yard at first light, June 1894
assets.provenance: Planned AI-assisted interpretive reconstruction; no claim that the scene is archival evidence.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Upper third flat overcast sky; lower-left unlit gravel for the three date lines.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve converging rails and both quiet type zones; no people or readable signage.

assets.subject: Stopped locomotive on a small-town siding at night with two or three familiar local figures in silhouette
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction of the Martinsburg stoppage atmosphere, not a likeness of specific participants.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Right half deep shadow for date stamp and body lines.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep locomotive stopped and figures close together rather than confrontational; protect right-side shadow.

assets.subject: Telegraph key and curling paper tape with an out-of-focus railroad map behind it
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction used as the substrate for the fourteen-day network instrument.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Entire upper half dark and undetailed; right edge quiet for counters.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep key and tape legible while leaving the map intentionally soft and all typography absent.

assets.subject: Morning-after burned Pittsburgh rail yard with a locomotive on its side, ash, smoke, and no people
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction informed by documented Pittsburgh strike damage figures; not archival evidence.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Left third flat smoke haze for the ledger panels.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve overturned locomotive and large scale of damage while keeping left third quiet.

assets.subject: Nineteenth-century urban National Guard armory facade built as a fortification
assets.provenance: Planned source-first visual. Prefer a real surviving period armory photograph with public-use clearance; the Hayes identity anchor may be supplied separately in-page if a reliable public-domain portrait is sourced.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Sky above roofline in upper quarter; lower-right shadowed brick for source quotation.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve fortress-like facade and quiet sky; avoid readable modern signage.

assets.subject: Iron-framed factory clock above a machine floor, photographed close with clouded glass
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction serving as the environmental substrate for the workday dial.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Full lower half blurred and dark for the dial; upper-left quiet for the date.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep clock dominant and machine floor abstract; no readable factory signage.

assets.subject: Wet cobblestone Haymarket square at night with gaslight and an empty speaker wagon, no crowd and no police
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction of place and atmosphere, explicitly not a depiction of the bombing.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Upper-right wet dark sky for timestamp; lower foreground stones for body lines.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve empty wagon and wet square while maintaining the two quiet type zones.

assets.subject: Courtroom evidence table viewed directly overhead with period documents and one shallow evidence box
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive legal-record substrate. Defendant likenesses are not fabricated; any identity anchors used in the page must come from reliable period visual sources.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Full frame kept low-contrast paper tone so the sortable record can occupy the table surface.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve broad empty paper substrate and overhead geometry rather than individual document details.

assets.subject: Empty nineteenth-century jail corridor with barred windows casting hard parallel light
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction of a jail corridor. It is environmental, not represented as the Cook County jail itself unless a verified source supports the architecture.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Lower-third floor bright and flat for three dated blocks.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep barred-window light geometry and empty corridor; protect lower-third floor.

assets.subject: Tall fortified wooden fence running along a riverbank at dusk with barbed wire, rifle ports, and mill silhouette
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction based on documented Fort Frick dimensions and features; not archival evidence.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Upper-third sky above fence; lower-left water for the vertical chain.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve length and defensive character of fence; keep sky and lower-left water quiet.

assets.subject: Monongahela River at dawn from water level with mist, a distant barge silhouette, and dark watching shoreline
assets.provenance: Planned interpretive reconstruction of the river approach, not a depiction of the fighting itself.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Mist band across middle for body lines; sky at top for date.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep barge at middle distance and shoreline watchfulness; protect mist band.

assets.subject: Straight-on row of Pullman company brick houses in flat afternoon light, empty and meticulously ordered
assets.provenance: Planned source-first treatment. Prefer verified Pullman housing visual evidence or a reconstruction that preserves documented architecture without pretending to be archival.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Lower-third pavement for ledger; flat sky above rooflines for heading.
assets.responsiveCrop: Preserve repetitive brick-house order and both type zones.

assets.subject: Single federal court document on a desk at a low raking angle with embossed seal and fountain pen
assets.provenance: Planned source-first legal-document treatment. Use authentic document visual evidence when available; otherwise use a clearly interpretive blank court-paper reconstruction with all readable language rendered separately in HTML.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Near-white paper surface across upper two thirds for stepped sequence.
assets.responsiveCrop: Keep seal, pen, and large quiet paper field; do not fabricate readable court text in the image.

assets.subject: Four flights of an iron stairwell photographed straight upward from the bottom, identical landings receding into light
assets.provenance: Planned editorial reconstruction used as a structural metaphor for the four-case ladder, not literal historical evidence.
assets.htmlSafeZone: Bright opening at top for header; stair treads remain legible enough to carry the fixed comparison rungs.
assets.responsiveCrop: Protect all four landings and upward geometry; preserve top opening.
